BOAS surgery for bulldogs

BOAS surgery for English bulldogs is a set of airway procedures, nostril widening and soft palate shortening, that reduces breathing effort in brachycephalic dogs. In Los Angeles it costs between 3,500 and 6,000 USD and most dogs go home the same day.

The procedure has two standard parts: alar fold resection to widen stenotic nares, and staphylectomy to shorten an elongated soft palate. Surgery takes forty-five to ninety minutes under general anaesthesia. In about thirty per cent of dogs a third step, removal of everted laryngeal saccules, is added when they obstruct the airway.

Most bulldogs breathe noticeably better within forty-eight hours and return to normal activity in fourteen days. Swelling of the soft palate peaks at twenty-four to seventy-two hours, which is why the first two nights are the highest risk period. Soft food for ten days and no collar pressure for two weeks are the two rules owners must follow.

Serious complications occur in fewer than five per cent of cases. The main risks are post-operative swelling, aspiration pneumonia and regurgitation during the first seventy-two hours. Older dogs and dogs with laryngeal collapse carry a higher risk.
